newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Malnutrition kills 1,000 Brazil children daily - group.
newsitem.headline: Malnutrition kills 1,000 Brazil children daily - group.

text.p: A welfare group backed by the United Nations launched a campaign on Tuesday against malnutrition, which it said kills 1,000 Brazilian children a day.

Carlos Eduardo Calfat-Salem, president of a foundation that bears his name, told reporters at least 12 million children suffered from lack of food in Latin America's largest country, where wealth distribution is one of the world's worst.
"The death rate is equivalent to the explosion of two Hiroshima atomic bombs every year. It's a massacre, a crime against humanity," Calfat-Salem said.

The private Calfat-Salem foundation, backed by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO), will distribute food to children at 30,000 churches throughout Brazil, he said.
The aim was to deliver "strong, healthy and intelligent children to public schools," Calfat-Salem said, criticising government food programmes as insufficient.
UNESCO Director General Federico Mayor said in a message to the foundation that the campaign had the organisation's full backing.
